text.p: A prominent Vietnamese dissident who was jailed for illegal possession and dissemination of state secrets has been released, the Foreign Ministry said on Monday.
"Nguyen Xuan Tu was sentenced by the Hanoi People's Court to one year in prison on the charge of intentionally disclosing state secrets," a ministry spokesman said in a statement.
"After finishing his term, he has been released and allowed to return to Dalat, Lam Dong, his former residence," he said.
Tu, a leading scientist and writer who is more commonly known as Ha Si Phu, was arrested in December last year while visiting relatives in Hanoi.
The Paris-based Alliance Vietnam Liberte (Free Vietnam Alliance) said in a statement that Tu was in a precarious state of health due to poor living conditions in prison.
But the Foreign Ministry said: "As far as we know, Tu's health is normal."

He was sentenced by the Hanoi People's Court in August along with former senior Communist Party member Le Hong Ha and Nguyen Kien Giang, former editor of a state publishing house and a longtime party critic.
The Hanoi Supreme Court last month rejected an appeal by Ha against his two-year prison sentence.
Hanoi has not specified the nature of the secrets involved.

But overseas Vietnamese human rights group say the three men were found in possession of a copy of a report by Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet to the Politburo in August 1995 which outlined the preparation strategy for this year's landmark party congress.
